title: Grade 8 Science — Mon, May 18
description: Crop Production & Management — Day 1 of 5: Agricultural practices and soil preparation
subject: science

questions.question: Crops that grow in summer (April–June) are called:
questions.explanation: Zaid crops grow in summer between Rabi and Kharif seasons (March–June). Examples: watermelon, cucumber, muskmelon.

questions.question: Kharif crops are sown in which season?
questions.explanation: Kharif crops are monsoon crops: sown at beginning of monsoon (June), harvested in autumn (September–October). Examples: rice, maize, cotton.

questions.question: Rabi crops grow in:
questions.explanation: Rabi crops: winter crops. Sown October–November, harvested March–April. Examples: wheat, gram, mustard, pea.

questions.question: The first step in preparing a field for cultivation is:
questions.explanation: Ploughing is the first step — it loosens the soil, allows air and water to penetrate, kills weeds, and brings nutrients to the surface.

questions.question: Which tool is traditionally used for ploughing?
questions.explanation: Traditional ploughing uses a wooden or iron plough pulled by bullocks. Modern farming uses iron ploughs or tractors.

questions.question: After ploughing, the soil is broken into smaller pieces. This process is called:
questions.explanation: After ploughing, harrowing breaks large clods into smaller pieces. The field is then levelled for uniform water distribution.

questions.question: Why is levelling of soil done after ploughing?
options: To make the field look neat
To prevent waterlogging, allow uniform irrigation, and destroy weeds
questions.explanation: Levelling prevents water from pooling in some areas. It distributes irrigation water evenly and exposes weed seeds to die.

questions.question: Good agricultural soil should:
options: Be compact and hard for root support
Be loose, well-aerated, rich in minerals and organic matter, with good water retention
questions.explanation: Ideal soil: loose (easy root penetration), aerated (oxygen for roots), mineral-rich (nutrients), organic matter (humus), retains some moisture.

questions.question: Organic matter (humus) in soil is important because:
options: It improves soil structure, water retention, and provides nutrients as it decomposes
It prevents microbes from living in soil
questions.explanation: Humus: improves soil texture, holds water, provides nutrients (N, P, K) when decomposed by microorganisms. Essential for fertile soil.

questions.question: Deep ploughing is preferred because:
options: It brings subsoil nutrients to the surface and allows deeper root growth
questions.explanation: Deep ploughing: brings lower-layer nutrients to topsoil, allows deeper root penetration, breaks hardpan (compacted layer), improves drainage.

questions.question: Which crop is a Kharif crop?
questions.explanation: Rice is a Kharif (monsoon) crop — it needs ample water. Wheat, mustard, and gram are Rabi (winter) crops.

questions.question: Which crop is a Rabi crop?
questions.explanation: Wheat is a classic Rabi crop (October–March). Cotton and maize are Kharif; sugarcane is grown almost year-round.

questions.question: Soil erosion can be prevented by:
options: Ploughing always in the direction of slope
Planting trees and cover crops (contour ploughing, terracing)
questions.explanation: Contour ploughing, terracing, planting trees/cover crops, and windbreaks prevent soil erosion by holding soil in place.

questions.question: The scientific study of agriculture is called:
questions.explanation: Agronomy is the science of soil management and crop production. Agricultural science covers all aspects of farming.

questions.question: Summary: the basic agricultural practices for crop production are:
options: Soil preparation (ploughing, harrowing, levelling), sowing, irrigation, fertilization, weeding, harvesting, storage
questions.explanation: Eight main agricultural practices: soil preparation → sowing → adding manure/fertilizer → irrigation → weeding → harvesting → threshing → storage.
